messages:
anya: Quick follow-up to the model-versioning RFC — we still need to settle the stable-binding metadata shape. Two choices I'm hearing: use content-hash as the canonical id, or maintain a semantic version tag + lease. Need to agree for rollout tooling and rollback semantics.

kai: I vote for hybrid: canonical_id = content_hash, plus optional semantic_tag. Keep canonical_id authoritative for routing, tag for humans. Also add a short compatibility_sig so we can quickly filter incompatible variants.

marcos: Hybrid makes sense but watch out: quantization and packaging can change the hash even when behavior is same. We should normalize the artifact (strip build-metadata) before hashing or use a fingerprint of model weights only. Otherwise tiny packaging diffs will break pins.

anya: Good point. Normalized-fingerprint + content-hash for full artifact? Which one is the single source of truth for bindings?

kai: Use normalized_fingerprint as binding key, and artifact_hash as release id. Normalized_fingerprint drives rollout affinity; artifact_hash is what we actually serve and is present in the rollout event.

sara: Tenant/data isolation concern: pinned artifacts linger in storage. We need TTL + owner field in metadata so private deploys can garbage-collect unused pins. Also, audit log reference required for compliance.

marcos: Agreed. Suggested metadata fields: 
```json
{
  "binding_key": "sha256:...",           // normalized fingerprint
  "artifact_hash": "sha256:...",        // exact artifact hash
  "semantic_tag": "v1.4.0",
  "compatibility_sig": "tokencount:2048|arch:llama2-13b:attn-checksum:...",
  "lease_expires_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z",
  "owner": "tenant-acme-corp",
  "gc_policy": "soft|hard",
  "note": "quantized build q4"
}
```

anya: That looks good. Two tradeoffs to call out: 1) fingerprinting step adds cost to model onboarding pipeline, 2) more metadata increases index size in the catalog service. Are we okay with both?

kai: Onboarding cost is acceptable; we already run validation and benchmarks. We can do fingerprinting asynchronously and mark artifacts as pending until fingerprint is ready. Index size — we can compress common fields and shard by tenant.

infra-bot: deploy-checks: model-catalog indexing benchmark: +45ms per artifact (median), storage +8% for metadata. No errors in 10k-run test.

marcos: Also consider fallback rules: if fingerprint mismatch on routing, fall back to "compatible_variant" lookup using compatibility_sig, then to semantic_tag, then to default model. Document ordering in rollout policy.

sara: For private deployments, owners may want to opt-out of automatic fallback. Add tenant_flag: allow_fallbacks = true/false.

anya: OK, action items: 1) I'll draft a short PR that implements normalized_fingerprint + artifact_hash + compatibility_sig fields and GC ttl/owner/gc_policy, 2) kai will update onboarding pipeline to emit fingerprint asynchronously, 3) marcos will write the routing fallback order doc. We aim to ship this to staging next sprint.

kai: Sounds good. If no objections by EOD, I'll start the PR. :thumbsup:

marcos: No objections from me.

sara: Fine by me, but please include the compliance audit fields.

anya: Thanks all — filing the RFC follow-up now and linking this thread.

infra-bot: Note: created issue #2345: "normalized-fingerprint + rollout metadata" (assignee: anya).
